sentence: A housefly beats its wings about two hundred times a second.
claim: Flies beat their wings roughly 140 to 200 times a second.
source_title: Kinematic diversity suggests expanded roles for fly halteres (wingbeat frequencies of many fly families), Biology Letters (2015)
status: OPEN: a person must open the link and check
note: Read the table: wingbeat frequencies of flies in this survey run from about 137 to about 200 Hz (blow flies about 160 to 200). A housefly was not read separately, so the script says "a fly" and "close to two hundred".
derivation: Flies beat their wings roughly 140 to 200 times a second (blow flies about 160 to 200); the film says "close to two hundred" for a fly.

sentence: Slow it a hundred times, and that's two beats a second.
claim: Slowed 100 times, a fly's 200-beat-a-second wing beats about twice a second on screen.
note: DERIVATION (our calculation, run it); no outside source.
derivation: About 200 / 100 = about 2 beats per second of screen time.

sentence: It hits, and the water climbs into a crown. The whole crown forms in a few hundredths of a second.
claim: A water drop landing in a thin layer of water throws up a crown within a few hundredths of a second.
source_title: Yarin, 'Drop impact dynamics: splashing, spreading, receding, bouncing', Annu. Rev. Fluid Mech. 38, 159 (2006)
note: FROM MEMORY, NOT OPENED (the builder recalled this; no source text was read this session); a person must open the source and check the number and the wording before posting. Crown timescales depend on drop size, speed and the liquid layer; 'a few hundredths of a second' is a hedge, not a measurement. LEAD: a search summary says the crown (corolla) emerges on the drop-film merger time scale of about 1 ms and grows over tens of milliseconds; the film says "a few hundredths", still unverified.
derivation: A falling water drop hitting a thin layer of water forms a crown within a few hundredths of a second (tens of milliseconds).

sentence: At this speed, that takes a few seconds.
claim: A few hundredths of a second, slowed 100 times, takes a few seconds on screen.
note: DERIVATION (our calculation, run it); no outside source.
derivation: A few hundredths of a second times 100 is a few seconds.

sentence: A mosquito's wings beat about five hundred times a second.
claim: Mosquitoes beat their wings several hundred times a second (about 340 to 740 in one survey; 500 is a round value).
source_title: Infrared light sensors permit rapid recording of wingbeat frequency and bioacoustic species identification of mosquitoes (Scientific Reports, 2021)
status: OPEN: a person must open the link and check
note: Read Table 1: mean wingbeat frequency of 29 North American mosquito species spans about 342 Hz (Culex restuans) to about 737 Hz; Aedes aegypti mean about 498 Hz. 500 is a fair round value.
derivation: Mosquito wingbeats are several hundred per second (reports range roughly 300 to 800); the film uses 500 as one round value.

sentence: Here, that's five beats a second.
claim: Slowed 100 times, a mosquito's 500 beats a second becomes 5 a second on screen.
note: DERIVATION (our calculation, run it); no outside source.
derivation: 500 beats a second / 100 = 5 beats per second of screen time.
